svg.title: How Auto-align gets the light back
svg.desc: Filled contour plot of the single-mode fiber coupling, as a share of the best, over M1X and M2X in microsteps from the peak, computed by the bench twin simulator, not measured. The high coupling is a long, thin ridge running diagonally across the plot. After M1 is knocked 1.2 mrad there is no light; a square spiral on M2 finds it on the ridge after 106 points and 14 s. Steer and walk then follows the ridge to the peak and ends at 99% of the best after 28 s. A 4 times zoom shows one motor at a time stalling partway along the ridge, at 83% after 20 s. A key shows walk, M1 plus an opposite M2 move, along the ridge, and steer, M2 alone, across it. Three steps: 1, find the light with a square spiral on M2, up to 0.4 turn either way by default, until out/ref clears 2% of its aligned value; 2, steer with M2 alone, the narrow direction, 1/e at 25 microsteps of M2X; 3, walk with M1 and an opposite M2 move, the wide direction, 1/e at 580 microsteps of M1X, repeated until a sweep gains less than 0.3%. Each line search approaches its points from one side, so the play in the hex couplings always sits the same way. In 100 simulated knocks of 0.3 to 3 mrad on a random mirror, at 60 RPM and 600 RPM/s, steer and walk brought 100 back above 99.9% of the best coupling, median 19 s, worst 66 s; one motor at a time brought 59 back to 90%, and the worst ended at 41%.
svg.text: How Auto-align gets the light back
For a single-mode fiber the peak is a ridge 23 times longer than it is wide, running diagonally across M1 and M2.
One motor at a time often stalls partway along it; steering and walking follow it, the way people align by hand.
square spiral on M2, up to ±0.4 turn
No light at the output: M2 steps
M2 alone, 1/e at 25 microsteps on M2X
M1 + opposite M2, 1/e at 580 on M1X
Keeps the spot still and turns only
Each line search approaches its points from one side,
so the play in the hex couplings always sits the same way.
steer + walk, back above 99.9% of the best
one motor at a time, back to 90%
